newsitem.title: USA: Oxy says expects to lift Cano force majeure.
newsitem.headline: Oxy says expects to lift Cano force majeure.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp expects to lift force majeure on the Cano Limon oil field in Colombia within 90 minutes, a company spokesman said on Friday.
Oxy plans to announce that it has lifted the measure after Ecopetrol announces that has lifted its force majeure on Cano Limon loadings.
"(Ecopetrol) is supposed to make an announcement within an hour," the spokesman said. "As soon as they announce that they have lifted force majeure, we will follow."

Oxy declared force majeure on the 175,000 barrel per day (bpd) field on July 15, the first time it has taken such as move on the field, following a string of rebel bombings of the Cano Limoon-Covenas pipeline.
State oil company Ecopetrol declared force majeure on loadings on July 6, a relatively common occurrence due to frequent rebel bombings of the pipeline.
The pipeline has a capacity to transport around 300,000 bpd of crude to the Caribbean port of Covenas.
Ecopetrol officials were not immediately available to comment.
Another Oxy spokesman said crude from the field had begun flowing again into Covenas.
"We have pressure at Covenas ... Things are starting to stabilize," he said.
He said Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline appeared to be back in full working order, a day after Ecopetrol technicians repaired damage from back-to-back bombings by leftist guerrillas.
Several oil companies have been shopping around for alternative crude supply in the wake of the shutdown in Colombia.
